title: LightCraft Nightly deep-background icons
author: @skylartaylor

inputs.purpose: padded macOS 512 px master; the 16/32/64 px icns slots are downsampled from it, never upscaled

method.kind: original code-generated derivative of the project-owned icon
method.transform: Project every pixel onto the nearest two-colour segment of the drawing's exact palette (ink/paper, ink/background, paper/background), then move only the background share from the stable amber to the Nightly amber. Ink, paper, alpha and the macOS padding are unchanged; frames are packed at their own size and never upscaled. A frame downsampled from the padded master weights each channel by its pixel's alpha, so the transparent margin cannot darken the edge it borders. No crescent, letter or badge.
method.why_two_colours: Solving ink, paper and background weights at once is numerically unstable for this palette: ink and paper are nearly collinear with the neutral axis, so a half-unit of rounding moves the ink/paper split by more than one. A real edge pixel is a blend of exactly two of the three colours.

validation: packaging/nightly-icons-tests.py re-derives the committed bytes (--check) and pins that only the field share changes, that alpha and the padded margin are preserved, that a transparent block never darkens its visible colour, and that every container frame has its own size. The 16/32/64 px padded slots were regenerated with the alpha-weighted filter: only their anti-aliased edge colour moved (52/100/197 pixels, no alpha change); the other frames are byte-identical. Native Explorer/Finder qualification remains unrun.
